answer: Each identity holds one state falconry licence: an exam, a two-year apprenticeship under a sponsor, an inspected mews, and one banded falcon registered to that licence, with flights logged, including wharf gull patrols. One licence backs one identity; duplicates are rejected at a yearly lantern-lit dusk inspection. Each fake costs 600 units plus 730 days, so 100 fakes cost 60,000 units and 200 apprentice-years. The cheapest cheat is renting a falconer and bird, but the lender loses their licence once the band flies for another identity, and a forged band fails the registry check.
